paper.title_en: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $Λ$CDM simulations
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $Λ$CDM expectations.
